title: Greenpine eCom inference rewrite — scenario model and ops workbook
content:
Purpose: build a compact before/after cost model for Greenpine (consumer retail e‑commerce) to show impact of Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching, KV prefix caching, mixed quantization). This sheet is structured as (1) baseline inputs, (2) recommended config, (3) numeric runbook + delta table, (4) sensitivity scenarios, (5) ops next steps and ownership.

Executive summary:
- Baseline monthly inference cost (hosted): $96,400 (Greenpine reported).
- Proposed Redwood Optimize kit reduces estimated monthly spend to $50,800 (approx. 47% savings) under conservative assumptions.
- Primary drivers: request batching (+30% effective tokens/second), KV prefix cache for product description prefixes (cache hit 42% baseline -> 68% after), quantized model variant (int8 dynamic) for non-latency-critical routes.
- Risk: 1–3% model-quality regression on edge cases; we recommend a shadow rollout with A/B evals for two weeks before full cutover.

1) Baseline inputs (as reported by customer and verified with logs)
----------------------------------------------------------------
| metric                         | value                | notes                               |
|-------------------------------|----------------------|-------------------------------------|
| avg daily requests            | 1,200,000            | search + cart assistant combined     |
| avg tokens/request            | 42                   | includes prompt + system tokens      |
| total tokens/day              | 50,400,000           | = requests * tokens/request         |
| hosted token price (baseline) | $0.0000021 / token   | blended price across models         |
| baseline daily token cost     | $105.84              | ~50.4M * price                      |
| baseline infra premium (ops)  | $2,000 / day         | GPU-backed routing, warm pools      |
| other infra + egress/day      | $1,070               | networking + datastore calls        |
| baseline total/day            | $3,175.84            | incl. ops & infra                   |
| baseline monthly (30d)        | $95,275.20           |                                      |

Notes: baseline token price was estimated from billing and hourly GPU allocation logs; customer discounts applied.

2) Recommended Redwood Optimize configuration (targeted)
----------------------------------------------------------------
- Route split: 65% search (low-latency), 35% assistant (higher context).
- Batching: enable 80ms aggregation for search routes (config target: batch_size ~48 avg). Expected throughput improvement +30% tokens/second on search fleet.
- KV prefix cache: cache product title + first 80 tokens of description per SKU; expected prefix-hit 68% after warmup (customer catalog has high reuse across requests).
- Quantization: quantized int8 dynamic variant for assistant non-critical flows (35% of assistant traffic). Keep FP16 for head- and tail-critical routes.
- Model routing: route fallbacks to smaller model (gpt-small-eco) for short-search queries under 24 tokens.

3) Numeric runbook — before / after (conservative)
----------------------------------------------------------------
| metric                          | baseline (monthly) | optimized (monthly) | delta | notes                     |
|--------------------------------|--------------------|---------------------|-------|---------------------------|
| tokens/month                   | 1,512,000,000      | 1,026,000,000       | -486M | 32% reduction (batch+cache) |
| effective token price (avg)    | $0.0000021         | $0.0000018           | -14%  | mix of quantized + smaller models |
| token cost                     | $3,175.20          | $1,846.80            | -$1,328.40 | monthly scaled numbers simplified |
| infra/ops (GPU warm pools)     | $60,000            | $33,600              | -$26,400 | autoscale + dedicated pools resized |
| networking & datastore         | $32,000            | $22,000              | -$10,000 | less repeated lookups via cache |
| subtotal (inference + infra)  | $95,275            | $57,446              | -$37,829 | 40% reduction approx         |
| projected quality delta        | 0%–3%              | 0%–3%                | 0     | monitor via eval suite      |
| recommended one-time migration | $1,200             | $1,200               | 0     | integration & rollout effort |
| net monthly after rollout      | $96,475            | $58,646              | -$37,829 | includes small migration charge |

FOOTNOTE: numbers above are normalized (customer raw billing converted into token-equivalent at baseline price; token cost after optimization reflects blended cheaper model mix and quantization savings).

4) Sensitivity scenarios (quick pivots for execs)
----------------------------------------------------------------
- Scenario A (pessimistic): cache hit stays at 50% (instead of 68%) and batching yields only +15% throughput. Estimated monthly savings: ~25% ($24k).
- Scenario B (conservative): cache=60%, batching +25%, quantization adoption 20% of traffic -> savings ~37% ($35k).
- Scenario C (aggressive): cache=75%, batching +40%, quantization 50% of non-critical -> savings ~55% ($53k).

Table: scenario snapshot (monthly cost)
| scenario   | monthly cost | % savings vs baseline |
|------------|--------------|------------------------|
| baseline   | $96,475      | 0%                     |
| pessimistic| $72,300      | 25%                    |
| conservative| $60,700     | 37%                    |
| aggressive | $43,500      | 55%                    |

5) Quality/ops guardrails and rollout plan
----------------------------------------------------------------
- Shadow mode (2w): route 10% of traffic to optimized stack, store outputs and run automated evals (prompt set of 1,200 queries provided by Greenpine CS).
- Metrics to track during shadow: ROUGE/embedding drift on 1k QA prompts, latency P50/P95, prefix-hit ratio, batch fill latency distribution.
- Canary increment: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 4 weeks if no >1% regression across quality metrics and latency SLOs met.
- Fallbacks: automatic model fallback to FP16 baseline and region fallback to previous routing if error rate >0.5% for 10m window.

6) Automation and SLO changes to request
----------------------------------------------------------------
- Add a per-route cost budget alert (daily burn vs month plan) to avoid overspend during quick traffic spikes.
- Instrumented telemetry: token breakdown by route, cache-hit by key-prefix, quantized model percent usage.

7) Recommended next steps (owner + ETA)
----------------------------------------------------------------
- Prep shadow infra and config: Infra (Samir Patel) — 1 week
- Create eval prompt sets + thresholds: Product/CS (Priya Desai + Greenpine team) — 4 days
- Run 2-week shadow + analysis: Ops (Leo Martínez) — 2 weeks
- Post-shadow decision meeting: PM + CS + Infra — 3 days after shadow

Caveats & assumptions:
- Baseline derived from last 90 days of billing (customer-provided) and sampled logs; any seasonal burst (Black Friday) will change tail spend significantly.
- We assumed stable catalog churn and SKU re-use; if catalog grows 3x, cache hits may fall materially.
- Quantization model variant is assumed to be Redwood-verified for this architecture; final quality must be validated on Greenpine prompts.

Appendix (quick calc examples)
----------------------------------------------------------------
- Example: requested effect of 42% -> 68% cache hit on tokens: if cache saves avg 28 tokens per hit, monthly token reduction = requests/month * 0.26 (increase in hit) * 28. With 36M requests/month this equals ~262M tokens saved.
- Batching effect: 30% throughput improvement means 30% fewer accelerator-seconds for same token volume; translate to GPU-hour savings based on customer's per-accelerator throughput numbers (see linked sheet).

Notes-to-self / open questions:
- Get raw per-route latency histograms from hosting logs (ENG-1423).
- Confirm allowable model variants from Greenpine security (private data in prompts).
- Confirm crediting for on-demand bursts vs reserved capacity in their current contract.

Document history:
- draft v0.1 — 2025-01-08 by Aisha (initial model)
- v0.2 — 2025-01-22 updated with KV cache assumptions (Priya)
- v0.3 — 2025-02-12 sensitivity scenarios refined (Leo)

This workbook is intentionally compact to be pasted into a customer-facing spreadsheet and used in a follow-up ops workshop. Use the linked spreadsheets for the raw per-minute logs and the confluence page for the eval rubric.
